summary.intent: Bootstrap the newly configured release-please system with correct version tags, fix an excessive changelog on PR #427, and implement a quick task to expose the API version on the /health endpoint while hardening the CI release pipeline.
summary.outcome: Successfully bootstrapped 15 release tags, aligned api-client versions with the API, added version to /health endpoint, and refactored the post-merge release workflow to commit release-as targets on the feature branch instead of pushing directly to main — avoiding branch protection bypass issues.

repo: release-please was set up in phase 41 with no prior tags, causing it to treat the entire commit history as unreleased — bootstrap tags at the pre-phase commit are required

extra-files paths in release-please-config.json are resolved relative to the package directory, not the repo root — packages/api-client/openapi.json under apps/api resolves to apps/api/packages/api-client/openapi.json (wrong); must use ../../packages/api-client/openapi.json or place under root package
Phase 41 discussion log (41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md line 106) specified monotonic (major.minor) versioning for Web and Desktop apps, but implementation used semver — user accepted semver for now
npm_package_version env var is not reliably set in all NestJS/ts-node execution contexts; reading package.json directly with fs.readFileSync + path.join is the safe fallback

The release-please PR only bumps files it knows about — it did not update openapi.json even with extra-files config because the path was wrong, causing the Verify API Spec & Client CI check to fail on the release PR
PR commits endpoint from GitHub API returns merge commits; these triggered false release labels across many packages in the pr-release-preview workflow — must filter commits with 2+ parents
post-merge workflow pushing release-as targets directly to main fails when branch protection requires status checks, even with bypass unchecked in legacy branch protection rules
Pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger new workflow runs — GitHub's built-in recursion prevention means no infinite loop risk when committing release-as from the preview workflow

code.finding: OpenAPI version was hardcoded as '0.1.0'; changed to read from process.env.npm_package_version with fs.readFileSync fallback on package.json; later refactored to import from shared src/version.ts

Same hardcoded '0.1.0' issue; also manually defines the /health endpoint spec because HealthController depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator and cannot be instantiated — the manual spec definition omitted version, error, and details fields that were added to the live controller
Extracted shared API_VERSION constant to avoid duplication between main.ts and health.controller.ts — reads npm_package_version env var with fs.readFileSync fallback

Manual override label preservation block did not feed the preserved higher bump back into packageBumps — release-as derivation used the lower computed bump instead of the manual label's bump; fixed by updating packageBumps for all paths mapped to that component via LABEL_TO_PATHS

release:none early return and release-as injection needed: (1) snapshot base branch config before clearing stale entries to avoid removing entries from previously merged PRs, (2) apply bump-minor-pre-major logic for 0.x packages on breaking changes, (3) preserve higher existing release-as targets rather than downgrading

extra-files entry for openapi.json was under apps/api package with path 'packages/api-client/openapi.json' — resolves relative to apps/api/, making it invalid; correct path is '../../packages/api-client/openapi.json'

workflow: commit type matters for release-please: fix: triggers patch bump, chore: does not trigger any bump — important when fixing CI/infra issues that shouldn't version-bump packages
When squash-merging branches with multiple commits, use git soft reset + recommit to rewrite all branch commits into a single correctly-scoped commit before force-pushing
GitHub Actions concurrency groups per PR (concurrency: group: pr-release-preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}) prevent race conditions when multiple commits push rapidly
Fork PRs should be guarded on steps that commit back to the PR branch — forks don't have write access, so the commit step needs: if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
re-enabling 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' in branch protection is safe once the CI pipeline no longer needs to push directly to main

friction: Branch protection 'Allow specified actors to bypass' is only available in the newer Rulesets UI, not legacy branch protection rules — caused multiple failed attempts to grant the release bot push access
Cargo.lock regeneration pulled in unrelated dependency updates when bumping crate versions — had to manually update only the specific crate entry with cargo update -p
git index.lock left behind by a crashed process blocked git operations — required manual removal
The gsd-executor was interrupted mid-run when the user wanted a different commit scope (feat(api): vs generic) — required reading the plan and executing the implementation manually
Web E2E test flakiness caused the release gate to fail on PR #430, requiring a manual re-trigger of the CI E2E workflow on main
OpenAPI extra-files jsonpath config silently failed — release-please gave no error but just didn't update the file, only discovered when the release PR's CI check failed
open_items: openapi.json extra-files path fix (../../packages/api-client/openapi.json) was committed but release-please PR #430 will need to be re-run or updated to pick up the corrected version

Release PR #430 changelog may still be incomplete — the post-merge targets job never successfully ran before the workflow was restructured; need to verify next release cycle works end-to-end with the new on-branch release-as approach
Phase 41 decision to use monotonic (major.minor) versioning for Web and Desktop apps was deferred — currently using semver; user accepted for now but noted it doesn't semantically fit end-user apps
Web E2E test flakiness is a recurring issue — the specific test failure in run 23829451742 was not root-caused, just accepted as flakiness

The 'Verify E2E Passed' check looks for the most recent run where Web E2E actually ran — this fallback logic could cause false failures whenever a CI run legitimately skips Web E2E due to no web changes
